examples.question_text:
(a) Write $13$ kilometres using the abbreviation, then change it to metres.
(b) Change $17000$ metres to kilometres.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $13$ kilometres $=13\text{ km}$
To change kilometres to metres, multiply by $1000$.
$13\times1000=13000$
$13\text{ km}=13000\text{ m}$
(b) To change metres to kilometres, divide by $1000$.
$17000\div1000=17$
$17000\text{ m}=17\text{ km}$

examples.question_text:
(a) Write $4287$ metres as kilometres and metres.
(b) Write $8$ kilometres $63$ metres using the abbreviations, then record the whole distance in metres.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $4287\text{ m}=4000\text{ m}+287\text{ m}$
$4000\text{ m}=4\text{ km}$
So $4287\text{ m}=4\text{ km }287\text{ m}$.
(b) $8$ kilometres $63$ metres $=8\text{ km }63\text{ m}$
$8\text{ km}=8000\text{ m}$
$8000\text{ m}+63\text{ m}=8063\text{ m}$

examples.question_text:
Order these distances from shortest to longest:
$5\text{ km }87\text{ m}$, $5136\text{ m}$, $4\text{ km }962\text{ m}$.
examples.solution_text:
Change all the distances to metres.
$5\text{ km }87\text{ m}=5000\text{ m}+87\text{ m}=5087\text{ m}$
$4\text{ km }962\text{ m}=4000\text{ m}+962\text{ m}=4962\text{ m}$
$4962<5087<5136$
From shortest to longest: $4\text{ km }962\text{ m}$, $5\text{ km }87\text{ m}$, $5136\text{ m}$.

examples.question_text: A route is $6\text{ km}$ long. After $3487\text{ m}$, how many metres remain?
examples.solution_text:
First change the whole distance to metres.
$6\text{ km}=6000\text{ m}$
$6000\text{ m}-3487\text{ m}=2513\text{ m}$
There are $2513\text{ m}$ left.

examples.question_text:
(a) Change $2.65\text{ km}$ to metres.
(b) Change $3840\text{ m}$ to kilometres.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Metres are smaller units, so multiply by $1000$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2.65\times1000\\&=2650\end{aligned}$
$2.65\text{ km}=2650\text{ m}$.
(b) Kilometres are larger units, so divide by $1000$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3840\div1000\\&=3.84\end{aligned}$
$3840\text{ m}=3.84\text{ km}$.
